title: Geometric fibre dimension bounds for algebraic spaces survive base change
statement: Algebraic spaces and their morphisms are as in [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]; their fibre products are [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. The topology on an algebraic space is the quotient topology from a surjective etale scheme atlas. Let $f:X\to B$ be a quasi-separated, locally finite type morphism from an algebraic space to a scheme $B$ [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]; locally finite type is tested on etale scheme charts, and quasi-separated means that the diagonal $X\to X\times_BX$ is quasi-compact (inverse images of quasi-compact opens are quasi-compact). Let $d\geq0$ be an integer. Assume that for each point $b\in B$, and an algebraic closure $\overline{\kappa(b)}$ of its residue field, the geometric fibre $X_{\bar b}=X\times_B\operatorname{Spec}\overline{\kappa(b)}$ has dimension at most $d$ [def-weil-geometric-fibre, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. For every morphism of schemes $B\prime\to B$, every geometric fibre of $X\times_BB\prime\to B\prime$ also has dimension at most $d$. The formula for the geometric fibre is the same sheaf fibre product when $X$ is an algebraic space; dimension is the Krull dimension of its underlying topological space. Empty and non-equidimensional fibres are allowed.

source.place: Tag 04NS, lemma-dimension-fibre-after-base-change, part (1), with definition-relative-dimension; the topological Krull dimension of a quasi-separated (hence decent) fibre equals its chart dimension by Tag 0A4J (decent-spaces.tex, lemma-dimension-decent-space).

proof.text: Fix $B\prime\to B$, a point $b\prime\in B\prime$, and an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\kappa(b\prime)$. Let $b$ be its image in $B$ and $k=\overline{\kappa(b)}$ the closure used in the hypothesis. The residue-field map followed by $\kappa(b\prime)\to\Omega$ embeds $\kappa(b)$ into $\Omega$. Since $k/\kappa(b)$ is algebraic and $\Omega$ is algebraically closed, the cited embedding lemma extends this map to $k\to\Omega$. Put $F=X\times_B\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $G=(X\times_B B\prime)\times_{B\prime}\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$. Associativity of sheaf fibre products identifies $G$ with $F\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$: on every test scheme both sides are pairs of a map to $X$ and a map to $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ whose maps to $B$ agree. Here [def-weil-geometric-fibre] specifies the chosen-closure formula for schemes; for $X$ an algebraic space we use precisely its sheaf-fibre-product extension stated in the item, not a claim that $F$ or $G$ is a scheme. Thus $\dim|F|\leq d$ by hypothesis, and it suffices to bound $\dim|G|$.

source.place: Tag 04NS, lemma-dimension-fibre-after-base-change (1), reduction to field fibres; field embedding supplied by fields.tex, algebraic-extension embedding into an algebraically closed extension

proof.text: Choose a representable surjective etale atlas $U\to X$ with $U$ a scheme. Let $V=U\times_B\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $W=U\times_B\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$. These are schemes and their maps $V\to F$ and $W\to G$ are surjective etale by the cited fibre-product and cover lemma. Fibre-product associativity gives $W\cong V\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$. Apply the atlas-dimension comparison to the quasi-separated morphism $f$ and separately the two scheme maps $\operatorname{Spec}k\to B$ and $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to B$. It gives $\dim|V|=\dim|F|\leq d$ and $\dim|W|=\dim|G|$. In the comparison input, quasi-separatedness is used over affine opens of each scheme test; this ensures Zariski local quasi-separatedness of the pulled-back space, without requiring the test scheme itself to be quasi-separated.

source.place: Tag 04NS proof, choice and pullback of scheme atlases; topological comparison: decent-spaces.tex Tag 0A4J and spaces-properties.tex Tag 0A4H

proof.text: If $W$ is empty, the conclusion follows from $\dim|G|=\dim|W|=-\infty\leq d$; hence assume $W$ nonempty. Its map to $V$ makes $V$ nonempty as well. By the chartwise locally-finite-type hypothesis, $U\to B$ is locally of finite type. The cited scheme base-change lemma makes $V\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ locally of finite type. By the definition of this property choose an affine open cover $V=\bigcup_i\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ with every $A_i$ a finite type $k$-algebra. The affine-cover dimension formula, together with the equality of topological scheme dimension and the supremum of local-ring dimensions, gives $\dim|V|=\sup_i\dim A_i$. Here ring dimension means the dimension of its prime spectrum. Therefore every $\dim\operatorname{Spec}A_i\leq d$.

source.place: Tag 04MU, lemma-dimension; locally-finite-type definition and its base change in morphisms.tex; reduction to finite type affine charts in algebra.tex Tag 00P3

proof.text: The inverse images of the opens $\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ cover $W$, since a point of $W$ maps to a point of $V$ in some member of its cover. The open-fibre-product lemma identifies the inverse image with $\operatorname{Spec}A_i\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$. The affine-spectra lemma identifies its ring with $A_i\otimes_k\Omega$. The maps $a\otimes\omega\mapsto\omega\otimes a$ and $\omega\otimes a\mapsto a\otimes\omega$ are inverse ring homomorphisms, since they preserve the balanced bilinear tensor relations and multiplication on pure tensors. Thus the inverse image is $\operatorname{Spec}(\Omega\otimes_k A_i)$ as an open subscheme of $W$. The field-extension dimension lemma applies to each $A_i$: it is finite type over the field $k$, and the embedding of step 1 makes $\Omega/k$ a field extension. It gives $\dim\operatorname{Spec}(\Omega\otimes_k A_i)=\dim\operatorname{Spec}A_i\leq d$.

source.place: Tag 00P3, lemma-dimension-preserved-field-extension; schemes.tex Tags 01JR and 01JQ for the open affine base-change charts

proof.text: Apply the affine-cover dimension formula and the scheme local-ring comparison to the nonempty scheme $W$ and the cover in step 4. Ring dimension is prime-spectrum dimension, so $\dim|W|=\sup_i\dim\operatorname{Spec}(\Omega\otimes_k A_i)\leq d$. Step 2 now gives $\dim|G|\leq d$. The choices of $B\prime$, $b\prime$, and its algebraic closure were arbitrary, proving the assertion. The empty case was treated in step 3, and no step requires components to have equal dimension.

proof_origin.place: Tag 04NS (1), atlas reduction specialized to geometric fibres; affine calculation supplied by algebra.tex Tag 00P3 and properties.tex Tag 04MU
